q1: SELECT b1.name AS bar1, b2.name AS bar2 FROM bar AS b1, bar AS b2 WHERE NOT EXISTS(SELECT s1.beer FROM serves AS s1 WHERE s1.bar = b1.name AND NOT EXISTS(SELECT 1 FROM serves AS s2 WHERE s2.bar = b2.name AND s2.beer = s1.beer)) AND EXISTS(SELECT s2.beer FROM serves AS s2 WHERE s2.bar = b2.name AND NOT EXISTS(SELECT 1 FROM serves AS s1 WHERE s1.bar = b1.name AND s1.beer = s2.beer))
q2: SELECT b1.bar, b2.bar FROM serves AS b1 JOIN serves AS b2 ON b1.bar <> b2.bar WHERE NOT EXISTS(SELECT * FROM serves AS s1 WHERE b1.bar = s1.bar AND NOT EXISTS(SELECT * FROM serves AS s2 WHERE s2.bar = b2.bar AND s1.beer = s2.beer))
q1_prompt_sql: SELECT b1.name AS bar1, b2.name AS bar2 FROM bar AS b1, bar AS b2 WHERE NOT EXISTS(SELECT s1.beer FROM serves AS s1 WHERE s1.bar = b1.name AND NOT EXISTS(SELECT 1 FROM serves AS s2 WHERE s2.bar = b2.name AND s2.beer = s1.beer)) AND EXISTS(SELECT s2.beer FROM serves AS s2 WHERE s2.bar = b2.name AND NOT EXISTS(SELECT 1 FROM serves AS s1 WHERE s1.bar = b1.name AND s1.beer = s2.beer))
q2_prompt_sql: SELECT b1.bar, b2.bar FROM serves AS b1 JOIN serves AS b2 ON b1.bar <> b2.bar WHERE NOT EXISTS(SELECT * FROM serves AS s1 WHERE b1.bar = s1.bar AND NOT EXISTS(SELECT * FROM serves AS s2 WHERE s2.bar = b2.bar AND s1.beer = s2.beer))
counterexample: INSERT INTO Bar (name, address) VALUES ('A', 'addressA'), ('B', 'addressB'); INSERT INTO Beer (name, brewer) VALUES ('X', 'brewerX'), ('Y', 'brewerY'); INSERT INTO Serves (bar, beer, price) VALUES ('A', 'X', 1.00), ('A', 'Y', 1.50), ('B', 'X', 1.00);
explanation: Q1 and Q2 are not equivalent. Q1 checks for bars that serve all the beers served by another bar and Q2 checks for bars that serve a beer that the other bar does not serve.
counterexample_dsp: Bar A serves beer X and beer Y. Bar B serves beer X. Bar A should be the result of Q1, but not of Q2.
